At first, only

can be selected, with the next option stating "Evolve Tonno Subito to unlock this form". When it evolves, it unlocks the next form and changes the next option from "???" to "Evolve ... to unlock this form" accordingly, following the order of the list above until all six forms are unlocked. Unlike other weapon selectors, the player is not given a choice in skipping weapons. Furthermore, the previous options can be picked again immediately, stacking the stats bonuses from leveling up. All six forms have a max level of six, and do not require passive items to evolve.
When Penshin Fatcha is picked again or evolved into, unlocked options can be picked immediately without having to start from Tonno Subito.
At the sixth evolution (which does not require unlocking all the options), a unique option appears.

The name Penshin Fatcha is a wordplay on "
", an idiom in Italian that means "a fish to the face", which means humiliating someone or treating them with malice or insensitivity.
"Tonno" means
in Italian. The first evolutions are all wordplays on that.
"Tonno Subito" means "instant tuna", it also sound similar to "Torno subito" which means "I'll be right back" in Italian.
"Tonnado" is a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "tornado".
"Tonn'omoto" can be a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "terremoto", Italian for "earthquake".
"Tonn'oddeeo" can be a wordplay on the words "tonno" and "oddeeo", which in English sounds like the Italian "Oddio!", meaning "Oh God!" or "Oh my goodness!"
"Tonne" is also a wordplay on the word "tonno" and the short form of the word "tonnellate", or "tons" in Italian.
"Unsurpassed" is a pun quoting "Tonno Insuperabile" (literally "Unsurpassed Tuna"), an Italian brand of canned tuna fish which had a very famous advertising in the '80s.
